segments.src: ## What a trade deficit actually is
segments.tr: ## What a trade deficit actually is

segments.src: The trade balance is the difference between what a country sells abroad (exports) and what it buys from abroad (imports).
segments.tr: The trade balance is the difference between what a country sells abroad (exports) and what it buys from abroad (imports).

segments.src: The figure covers both **goods**, such as vehicles, machinery, energy, and consumer products, and **services**, such as travel, transportation, financial services, and intellectual property licensing.
segments.tr: The figure covers both **goods**, such as vehicles, machinery, energy, and consumer products, and **services**, such as travel, transportation, financial services, and intellectual property licensing.

segments.src: When imports exceed exports, the result is a deficit.
segments.tr: When imports exceed exports, the result is a deficit.

segments.src: A $105.0 billion deficit means that, in that month, the value of what Americans and American businesses bought from the rest of the world was about $105 billion higher than the value of what the rest of the world bought from them.
segments.tr: A $105.0 billion deficit means that, in that month, the value of what Americans and American businesses bought from the rest of the world was about $105 billion higher than the value of what the rest of the world bought from them.

segments.src: The word "deficit" can be misleading.
segments.tr: The word "deficit" can be misleading.

segments.src: It is not a budget shortfall, and it is not debt in the way a household owes a bank.
segments.tr: It is not a budget shortfall, and it is not debt in the way a household owes a bank.

segments.src: It is a flow measurement: a monthly comparison of two streams of spending.
segments.tr: It is a flow measurement: a monthly comparison of two streams of spending.

segments.src: ## Why a narrower gap is not automatically good or bad
segments.tr: ## Why a narrower gap is not automatically good or bad

segments.src: A smaller deficit can happen for very different reasons, and those reasons matter more than the direction of the number.
segments.tr: A smaller deficit can happen for very different reasons, and those reasons matter more than the direction of the number.

segments.src: **Potentially encouraging causes:**
segments.tr: **Potentially encouraging causes:**

segments.src: - Exports rise because foreign demand for U.S. farm products, energy, aircraft, or services increases.
segments.tr: - Exports rise because foreign demand for U.S. farm products, energy, aircraft, or services increases.

segments.src: - Domestic producers supply more of what buyers previously had to import.
segments.tr: - Domestic producers supply more of what buyers previously had to import.

segments.src: **Potentially less encouraging causes:**
segments.tr: **Potentially less encouraging causes:**

segments.src: - Imports fall because households and businesses are buying less overall, which can signal softer demand.
segments.tr: - Imports fall because households and businesses are buying less overall, which can signal softer demand.

segments.src: - Shipping disruptions or port delays temporarily hold back the arrival of goods.
segments.tr: - Shipping disruptions or port delays temporarily hold back the arrival of goods.

segments.src: - A previous surge of imports, perhaps from businesses stocking up ahead of price changes, simply reverses.
segments.tr: - A previous surge of imports, perhaps from businesses stocking up ahead of price changes, simply reverses.

segments.src: The same $105.0 billion figure could reflect any of these.
segments.tr: The same $105.0 billion figure could reflect any of these.

segments.src: That is why analysts look at the components, not just the total.
segments.tr: That is why analysts look at the components, not just the total.

segments.src: ## What drives imports and exports
segments.tr: ## What drives imports and exports

segments.src: Several broad forces shape trade flows:
segments.tr: Several broad forces shape trade flows:

segments.src: 1. **Relative economic strength.** When U.S. consumers and companies are spending confidently, they tend to buy more imported goods. When major trading partners grow more slowly, they may buy fewer U.S. exports.
segments.tr: 1. **Relative economic strength.** When U.S. consumers and companies are spending confidently, they tend to buy more imported goods. When major trading partners grow more slowly, they may buy fewer U.S. exports.

segments.src: 2. **Exchange rates.** A stronger dollar makes imports cheaper for Americans and U.S. exports more expensive for foreign buyers, which tends to widen the deficit over time. A weaker dollar works in the opposite direction, though with a lag.
segments.tr: 2. **Exchange rates.** A stronger dollar makes imports cheaper for Americans and U.S. exports more expensive for foreign buyers, which tends to widen the deficit over time. A weaker dollar works in the opposite direction, though with a lag.

segments.src: 3. **Prices.** Trade figures are measured in dollar values. If oil or other commodity prices change, the value of trade shifts even when the physical volume does not.
segments.tr: 3. **Prices.** Trade figures are measured in dollar values. If oil or other commodity prices change, the value of trade shifts even when the physical volume does not.

segments.src: 4. **Policy and supply chains.** Tariffs, trade agreements, and changes in where companies source their products can reroute trade between countries and shift timing.
segments.tr: 4. **Policy and supply chains.** Tariffs, trade agreements, and changes in where companies source their products can reroute trade between countries and shift timing.

segments.src: 5. **Seasonal and calendar effects.** Holiday buying seasons and shipping schedules create patterns that statisticians try to smooth out with seasonal adjustment.
segments.tr: 5. **Seasonal and calendar effects.** Holiday buying seasons and shipping schedules create patterns that statisticians try to smooth out with seasonal adjustment.

segments.src: ## Why the number swings from month to month
segments.tr: ## Why the number swings from month to month

segments.src: Monthly trade data is volatile.
segments.tr: Monthly trade data is volatile.

segments.src: A few large transactions, such as a batch of aircraft deliveries, can move the total noticeably.
segments.tr: A few large transactions, such as a batch of aircraft deliveries, can move the total noticeably.

segments.src: Shipments that cross a month boundary by a few days can make one month look unusually strong and the next unusually weak.
segments.tr: Shipments that cross a month boundary by a few days can make one month look unusually strong and the next unusually weak.

segments.src: Statistical agencies also revise earlier figures as more complete information arrives, so a number reported today may be adjusted later.
segments.tr: Statistical agencies also revise earlier figures as more complete information arrives, so a number reported today may be adjusted later.

segments.src: Because of this, economists tend to focus on **three-month or longer averages** rather than any single reading.
segments.tr: Because of this, economists tend to focus on **three-month or longer averages** rather than any single reading.

segments.src: A drop from a larger deficit to $105.0 billion is informative, but it is more meaningful if it is part of a sustained pattern.
segments.tr: A drop from a larger deficit to $105.0 billion is informative, but it is more meaningful if it is part of a sustained pattern.

segments.src: ## How trade feeds into GDP
segments.tr: ## How trade feeds into GDP

segments.src: Gross domestic product, the broadest measure of the size of the economy, includes net exports as one of its components, alongside consumer spending, business investment, and government spending.
segments.tr: Gross domestic product, the broadest measure of the size of the economy, includes net exports as one of its components, alongside consumer spending, business investment, and government spending.

segments.src: In the accounting, **exports add to GDP and imports subtract from it**.
segments.tr: In the accounting, **exports add to GDP and imports subtract from it**.

segments.src: This leads to a common misunderstanding.
segments.tr: This leads to a common misunderstanding.

segments.src: Imports are subtracted in the formula because they represent spending on goods produced elsewhere, but that spending is also counted in consumption or investment.
segments.tr: Imports are subtracted in the formula because they represent spending on goods produced elsewhere, but that spending is also counted in consumption or investment.

segments.src: Higher imports do not mean the economy is "losing" output.
segments.tr: Higher imports do not mean the economy is "losing" output.

segments.src: They simply offset the portion of domestic spending that went to foreign production.
segments.tr: They simply offset the portion of domestic spending that went to foreign production.

segments.src: Still, in the quarter-by-quarter accounting, a narrowing deficit generally gives GDP growth a mathematical lift, and a widening one weighs on it.
segments.tr: Still, in the quarter-by-quarter accounting, a narrowing deficit generally gives GDP growth a mathematical lift, and a widening one weighs on it.

segments.src: That is why trade reports often prompt forecasters to revise their estimates for economic growth.

segments.src: ## A balanced way to read the headline
segments.tr: ## A balanced way to read the headline

segments.tr: When you see a number like $105.0 billion, a few questions help put it in context:

us-20261111-consumer-advertising-psychol.title: [علم نفس المستهلك #3] لماذا تعلق تلك الجingle في رأسك: كيف يتعلم المستهلكون العلامات التجارية ويتذكرونها

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > تعلّمنا العلامات التجارية من خلال الاقترانات المتكررة والمكافآت، وسواء تذكّرنا علامة تجارية من تلقاء أنفسنا أم عرفناها فقط عند رؤيتها على الرف، فإن ذلك يغيّر طريقة شرائنا.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: لا أحد يولد وهو يعرف أن اللون الأحمر يعني "منعشًا" أو أن الشعار المنسدل يعني "رياضيًا".

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: نحن **نتعلم** هذه الروابط، معظمها دون أن نسعى إلى ذلك.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: يصف علماء نفس المستهلك هذا التعلم عادةً بطريقتين.

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: **الإشراط الكلاسيكي: التعلم بالترابط**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: في تجارب إيفان بافلوف الشهيرة، كانت الكلاب تسمع صوتًا مباشرةً قبل أن تحصل على الطعام.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: وبعد تكرار الاقتران عددًا كافيًا من المرات، كان الصوت وحده يكفي لجعلها تسيل لعابها.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: غالبًا ما تعمل الإعلانات وفق المبدأ نفسه.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: عندما تُعرض علامة تجارية (وهي مثير محايد) بجانب شيء يبعث بالفعل على الارتياح لدى الناس، مثل موسيقى مبهجة أو جرو لطيف أو مشهور يبتسم، فقد ينتقل جزء من ذلك الشعور الإيجابي إلى العلامة التجارية.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: يساعد التكرار، لكن التكرار المفرط قد يسبب *الإنهاك*، أي النقطة التي يشعر عندها الناس بالملل أو الضيق.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: وهناك فكرة مرتبطة بذلك هي **تعميم المثير**: إذ ينقل الناس مشاعرهم تجاه شيء ما إلى الأشياء التي تشبهه.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: ولهذا تستخدم العلامات التجارية الخاصة بالمتاجر غالبًا تغليفًا يشبه تغليف الرائد في السوق، ولهذا قد تطلق علامة تجارية معروفة خطًا جديدًا من المنتجات تحت الاسم نفسه.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: **الإشراط الإجرائي (الأداتي): التعلم من خلال النتائج**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: هنا يتشكل السلوك بحسب ما يحدث *بعده*.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: إذا أدّى شراء شيء ما إلى مكافأة، مثل منتج ممتاز أو خصم أو نقاط ولاء، فإنك تصبح أكثر ميلًا إلى شرائه مرة أخرى.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: وبرامج الولاء، وبطاقات "القهوة العاشرة مجانًا"، والمزايا المفاجئة كلها مبنية على هذا المبدأ.

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **الذاكرة: الاسترجاع مقابل

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: التعرّف**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: لا يكون التعلم مهمًا إلا إذا بقي في الذاكرة.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: يميّز المسوّقون بين نوعين من ذاكرة العلامة التجارية:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **استرجاع العلامة التجارية**: أن تستحضر اسم العلامة بنفسك دون أي تلميح. ("اذكر تطبيقًا لمشاركة الرحلات.")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **التعرّف على العلامة التجارية**: أن تُعرّف على العلامة عندما تراها أو تسمعها. ("هل رأيت هذا الشعار من قبل؟")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: التعرّف أسهل من الاسترجاع.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: يتعرّف معظم الناس على عدد من العلامات يفوق بكثير ما يستطيعون تسميته دون تلميح.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: أيهما أهم يعتمد على المكان الذي تتخذ فيه قرارك.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: إذا كنت تختار أمام رف في المتجر، فقد يكفي التعرّف.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: أما إذا قررت قبل أن تخرج، كأن تختار مطعمًا أو تتصل بسبّاك، فيجب أن تخطر العلامة ببالك من تلقاء نفسها، لذلك يكون الاسترجاع هو الأهم.

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: وتُسمّى العلامات القليلة التي تخطر ببالك لفئة معينة أحيانًا **مجموعة الاعتبار**.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: تخيّل أنها ليلة الجمعة، ويرسل لك صديق رسالة: "هل نطلب بيتزا؟"

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: قبل أن تفتح أي تطبيق، تفكّر في ربما سلسلتين أو ثلاث سلاسل.

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: هذا هو **الاسترجاع** في عمله، والعلامات التي تخطر ببالك تحصل على الفرصة الأولى لإنفاق الـ 25 دولارًا.

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: تخيّل نفسك الآن في ممر الحبوب في متجر Target.

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: لم تكن قد خططت لعلامة بعينها، لكن علبة مألوفة تلفت انتباهك فتفكر: "آه، أعرف هذه."

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: هذا هو **التعرّف**، وللتغليف المألوف فرصة جيدة للفوز حتى لو لم تكن قادرًا على تسميته قبل ساعة.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: ثم هناك تطبيق مقهى يمنحك مشروبًا مجانيًا بعد عدد معين من المشتريات.

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: كل ختم أو نقطة مكافأة صغيرة تدفعك للعودة، وهذا هو الإشراط الإجرائي في جيبك.

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: أضف إلى ذلك إعلانًا موسميًا مبهجًا بموسيقى دافئة وأوراق الخريف، فيكون الإشراط الكلاسيكي يساعد أيضًا.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص في ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. يربط الإشراط الكلاسيكي العلامة التجارية بالمشاعر من خلال اقترانها المتكرر بشيء يحبه الناس أصلًا.

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. يشكّل الإشراط الإجرائي تكرار الشراء من خلال مكافآت مثل الجودة والخصومات ونقاط الولاء.

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. الاسترجاع (تسمية العلامة دون تلميح) أصعب من التعرّف (معرفتها عند رؤيتها)، وأيهما أهم يعتمد على مكان اتخاذ القرار.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.src: **Q1.** A soda ad always shows the brand alongside friends laughing at a summer barbecue, hoping viewers will feel happy about the brand.
segments.tr: **س1.** يعرض إعلان مشروب غازي دائمًا العلامة بجانب أصدقاء يضحكون في شواء صيفي، على أمل أن يشعر المشاهدون بالسعادة تجاه العلامة.

segments.src: This mainly uses:
segments.tr: وهذا يعتمد أساسًا على:

segments.src: - (a) Operant conditioning
segments.tr: - (أ) الإشراط الإجرائي

segments.src: - (b) Classical conditioning
segments.tr: - (ب) الإشراط الكلاسيكي

segments.src: - (c) Brand recall testing
segments.tr: - (ج) اختبار استرجاع العلامة التجارية

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X: For most people, brand recognition is harder than brand recall.
segments.tr: **س2.** صح/خطأ: بالنسبة لمعظم الناس، التعرّف على العلامة التجارية أصعب من استرجاعها.

segments.src: **Q3.** For which purchase is unprompted brand **recall** most important?
segments.tr: **س3.** في أي عملية شراء يكون **استرجاع** العلامة دون تلميح هو الأهم؟

segments.src: - (a) Grabbing gum at the checkout counter
segments.tr: - (أ) التقاط علكة عند منضدة الدفع

segments.src: - (b) Choosing a shampoo while scanning a store shelf
segments.tr: - (ب) اختيار شامبو أثناء تصفح رف في المتجر

segments.src: - (c) Deciding which insurance company to call before searching anywhere
segments.tr: - (ج) تحديد شركة التأمين التي ستتصل بها قبل البحث في أي مكان

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Classical conditioning**: Learning that happens when a neutral stimulus (like a brand) is repeatedly paired with one that already triggers a response.
segments.tr: - **الإشراط الكلاسيكي**: تعلّم يحدث عندما يُقترن مثير محايد (مثل علامة تجارية) بشكل متكرر بمثير يثير استجابة بالفعل.

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **الإشراط الإجرائي**: تعلّم يصبح فيه السلوك أكثر احتمالًا أو أقل بحسب المكافأة أو العقاب الذي يليه.

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **تعميم المثير**: الاستجابة لمثير يشبه الأصل بالطريقة نفسها، مثل الثقة بعبوة تشبه عبوة أخرى.

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.

us-20261111-news-1.title: الرفع بينما ينتظر الآخرون: لماذا يرفع بنك إنجلترا وأستراليا أسعار الفائدة مرة أخرى

segments.src: For much of the past two years, the global story in monetary policy was about cutting.
segments.tr: طوال الجزء الأكبر من العامين الماضيين، كانت القصة العالمية في السياسة النقدية تدور حول خفض الفائدة.

segments.src: Now a few central banks are moving the other way.
segments.tr: الآن تتجه بعض البنوك المركزية في الاتجاه المعاكس.

segments.src: The Bank of England has raised its benchmark rate to 4%, its first increase in more than three years.
segments.tr: رفع بنك إنجلترا سعره القياسي إلى 4٪، وهي زيادته الأولى في أكثر من ثلاث سنوات.

segments.src: The Reserve Bank of Australia has tightened five times this year.
segments.tr: قام بنك الاحتياطي الأسترالي بالتشديد خمس مرات هذا العام.

segments.src: This article explains what is behind those decisions and what they could mean for U.S.
segments.tr: تشرح هذه المقالة ما وراء تلك القرارات وما يمكن أن تعنيه للقراء في الولايات المتحدة.

segments.src: readers.
*This is general information and not investment or financial advice.
segments.tr: *هذه معلومات عامة وليست نصيحة استثمارية أو مالية.

segments.src: Details of policy decisions can change quickly, so check official central bank statements for the latest figures.*
segments.tr: يمكن أن تتغير تفاصيل قرارات السياسة بسرعة، لذا تحقق من البيانات الرسمية للبنوك المركزية لمعرفة أحدث الأرقام.*

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## ماذا حدث

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **المملكة المتحدة:** رفع بنك إنجلترا سعر السياسة إلى 4٪. هذه هي أول زيادة في أسعار الفائدة منذ أكثر من ثلاث سنوات، وهي تنهي فترة توقعت فيها الأسواق في الغالب إجراء تخفيضات.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **أستراليا:** رفع بنك الاحتياطي الأسترالي أسعار الفائدة خمس مرات هذا العام. وهذا يجعله أحد أكثر البنوك المركزية تشديداً نشاطاً بين الاقتصادات المتقدمة.

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: قال البنكان إن قراراتهما تتبع البيانات.

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: لم يصف أي منهما ذلك بأنه انحراف عن أهداف التضخم الخاصة بهما.

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: يقول كل منهما أنه يحاول إعادة التضخم نحو هدفه.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## لماذا يتسارع التضخم من جديد

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: نادراً ما يرتفع التضخم لسبب واحد.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: يتم الاستشهاد بعدة قوى عادة في حالات مثل هذه:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **أسعار الخدمات اللاصقة.** تميل الأجور والإيجارات وتكاليف التأمين إلى التحرك ببطء. عندما تستمر في الارتفاع، يكون التضخم الرئيسي بطيئاً في التراجع.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **تكاليف الطاقة والغذاء.** يمكن تقلبات أسعار الطاقة والغذاء أن ترفع التضخم بسرعة. كما أنها تؤثر على ما تتوقع الأسر أن يكون عليه التضخم.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **أسواق العمل الضيقة.** في الأماكن التي لا يزال أصحاب العمل يعانون فيها من أجل التوظيف، يمكن أن يظل نمو الأجور مرتفعاً بما يكفي للحفاظ على الضغط على الأسعار.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **توقعات التضخم.** إذا توقعت الأسر والشركات ارتفاع الأسعار، فقد تحدد الأجور والأسعار وفقاً لذلك. تريد البنوك المركزية وقف هذه الدورة مبكراً.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **تحركات العملة.** العملة المحلية الأضعف تجعل الواردات أكثر تكلفة، مما يمكن أن يتدفق إلى أسعار المستهلك.

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: أي من هذه الأمور يهم أكثر يختلف حسب البلد.

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: هذا أحد الأسباب التي تجعل البنوك المركزية لا تتحرك كلها في نفس الوقت.

segments.src: ## Why some banks hike while others wait
segments.tr: ## لماذا ترفع بعض البنوك الفائدة بينما ينتظر البعض الآخر

segments.src: Central banks answer to different data.
segments.tr: تستجيب البنوك المركزية لبيانات مختلفة.

segments.src: A bank that sees inflation staying above target, or rising again, may judge that waiting is riskier than acting.
segments.tr: البنك الذي يرى التضخم يظل أعلى من المستهدف، أو يرتفع مرة أخرى، قد يقدّر أن الانتظار أكثر خطورة من العمل.

segments.src: A bank that sees slowing growth and cooling prices may choose to hold.
segments.tr: البنك الذي يرى تباطؤ النمو وتراجع الأسعار قد يختار التثبيت.

segments.src: Rate increases also carry costs.
segments.tr: زيادات أسعار الفائدة تحمل أيضاً تكاليف.

segments.src: Higher borrowing costs weigh on mortgage holders, small businesses and government budgets.
segments.tr: تؤثر تكاليف الاقتراض المرتفعة على أصحاب الرهن العقاري والشركات الصغيرة وموازنات الحكومات.

segments.src: Policymakers weigh those costs against the risk of letting inflation settle at a higher level.
segments.tr: يزن صانعو السياسات تلك التكاليف مقابل خطر السماح بتستقر التضخم عند مستوى أعلى.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar
segments.tr: ## ماذا يمكن أن يعني ذلك بالنسبة للدولار

segments.src: Exchange rates reflect the gap between interest rates in different places.
segments.tr: تعكس أسعار الصرف الفجوة بين أسعار الفائدة في أماكن مختلفة.

segments.src: When other central banks raise rates while the Federal Reserve holds steady, the difference narrows.
segments.tr: عندما ترفع البنوك المركزية الأخرى أسعار الفائدة بينما يحافظ الاحتياطي الفيدرالي على ثباته، يضيق الفرق.

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: يمكن أن يجعل ذلك العملات الأخرى أكثر جاذبية نوعاً ما مقارنة بالدولار.

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: تجدر الإشارة إلى عدة نقاط:

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.
segments.tr: - تعتمد تحركات العملة على عوامل عديدة، وليس فقط فروق أسعار الفائدة. وتشمل هذه النمو، وتدفقات التجارة، وشهية المستثمرين للمخاطرة.

segments.src: - The dollar often strengthens during periods of global uncertainty, which can offset the effect of narrower rate gaps.
segments.tr: - غالباً ما يرتفع الدولار خلال فترات عدم اليقين العالمي، مما يمكن أن يعوض تأثير فجوات أسعار الفائدة الضيقة.

segments.src: - Markets usually price in expected moves before they happen. A rate rise that was widely expected may have little effect on the day.
segments.tr: - عادة ما تسعر الأسواق التحركات المتوقعة قبل حدوثها. إن زيادة أسعار الفائدة التي كان متوقعة على نطاق واسع قد يكون لها تأثير ضئيل في ذلك اليوم.

segments.src: ## Import prices and everyday costs
segments.tr: ## أسعار الواردات والتكاليف اليومية

segments.src: A softer dollar makes imported goods more expensive for U.S.
segments.tr: الدولار الأضعف يجعل السلع المستوردة أكثر تكلفة للمشترين في الولايات المتحدة.

segments.src: - Electronics, vehicles and parts, and other manufactured goods
segments.tr: - الإلكترونيات، والمركبات وقطع الغيار، وغيرها من السلع المصنعة

segments.src: The effect is usually gradual.
segments.tr: يكون التأثير تدريجياً عادة.

segments.src: Retailers often hold prices for a while, and many firms hedge currency risk.
segments.tr: غالباً ما تحافظ تجار التجزئة على الأسعار لفترة من الوقت، وتقوم العديد من الشركات بتحوط مخاطر العملة.

segments.src: Any pass-through to consumer prices also depends on competition and demand.
segments.tr: أي انتقال إلى أسعار المستهلك يعتمد أيضاً على المنافسة والطلب.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the Fed
segments.tr: ## ماذا يمكن أن يعنيه ذلك بالنسبة للفيدرالي

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets policy based on U.S.
segments.tr: يحدد الاحتياطي الفيدرالي السياسة بناءً على ظروف الولايات المتحدة.

segments.src: conditions.
segments.tr: conditions.

segments.tr: تحركات أسعار الفائدة الأجنبية ليست مدخلاً مباشراً لقراراته.

segments.src: They can still matter in indirect ways:
segments.tr: لكنها لا تزال تهم بطرق غير مباشرة:

segments.src: - **Inflation signals.** If global price pressures are rising, it may be a warning for U.S. import prices and inflation expectations.
segments.tr: - **إشارات التضخم.** إذا كانت ضغوط الأسعار العالمية في ارتفاع، فقد تكون تحذيراً لأسعار الواردات الأمريكية وتوقعات التضخم.

segments.src: - **Financial conditions.** A weaker dollar loosens financial conditions a little. That could be a factor if the Fed wants to keep policy tight enough to bring inflation down.
segments.tr: - **الظروف المالية.** الدولار الأضعف يخفف الظروف المالية قليلاً. قد يكون ذلك عاملاً إذا أراد الاحتياطي الفيدرالي إبقاء السياسة مشددة بما يكفي خفض التضخم.

segments.src: - **Market expectations.** Investors often compare central banks. Moves abroad can change how markets price the path of U.S. rates.
segments.tr: - **توقعات السوق.** غالباً ما يقارن المستثمرون البنوك المركزية. يمكن أن تغير التحركات في الخارج كيف تسعر الأسواق مسار أسعار الفائدة الأمريكية.

segments.src: ## The bottom line

us-20261111-news-2.title: Few Layoffs, Few Hires: What Record-Low Jobless Claims Do and Don't Tell You

segments.src: Weekly jobless claims have recently sat near the lowest levels seen in decades.
segments.tr: Weekly jobless claims have recently sat near the lowest levels seen in decades.

segments.src: Yet many job seekers describe a market that feels slow: fewer openings, longer searches, and more rounds of interviews.
segments.tr: Yet many job seekers describe a market that feels slow: fewer openings, longer searches, and more rounds of interviews.

segments.src: This article explains why the layoff data and the hiring data can point in different directions, and which indicators help fill in the rest of the picture.

segments.src: ## What jobless claims actually measure
segments.tr: ## What jobless claims actually measure

segments.src: Initial jobless claims count the number of people who file for unemployment insurance benefits for the first time in a given week.
segments.tr: Initial jobless claims count the number of people who file for unemployment insurance benefits for the first time in a given week.

segments.src: The figure is published weekly by the U.S.

segments.src: Department of Labor, which makes it one of the fastest-moving signals about the labor market.

segments.src: That speed is its strength.
segments.tr: That speed is its strength.

segments.src: It is also its limit.
segments.tr: It is also its limit.

segments.src: Claims capture **layoffs**, meaning people who lose a job and apply for benefits.
segments.tr: Claims capture **layoffs**, meaning people who lose a job and apply for benefits.

segments.src: They say very little about:
segments.tr: They say very little about:

segments.src: - **Hiring**: how many people are being brought on.

segments.src: - **Quits**: workers who leave voluntarily and generally do not qualify for benefits.
segments.tr: - **Quits**: workers who leave voluntarily and generally do not qualify for benefits.

segments.tr: - **Eligibility gaps**: some workers do not qualify for benefits, and some who qualify never file.

segments.tr: It does not mean many people are being pulled into new ones.

segments.src: ## Why layoffs and hiring can diverge
segments.tr: ## Why layoffs and hiring can diverge

segments.src: ### Employers are holding on to workers
segments.tr: ### Employers are holding on to workers

segments.src: After the staffing shortages of recent years, many employers became wary of letting people go.
segments.tr: After the staffing shortages of recent years, many employers became wary of letting people go.

segments.src: Recruiting and training are expensive, and companies that struggled to fill roles may prefer to keep existing staff even when demand softens.
segments.tr: Recruiting and training are expensive, and companies that struggled to fill roles may prefer to keep existing staff even when demand softens.

segments.src: That keeps layoffs low.
segments.tr: That keeps layoffs low.

segments.src: ### Caution slows hiring at the same time
segments.tr: ### Caution slows hiring at the same time

segments.src: The same caution that discourages layoffs can discourage new hiring.
segments.tr: The same caution that discourages layoffs can discourage new hiring.

segments.src: When businesses are unsure about interest rates, costs, or future demand, a common response is to freeze headcount: don't cut, but don't add.
segments.tr: When businesses are unsure about interest rates, costs, or future demand, a common response is to freeze headcount: don't cut, but don't add.

segments.src: The result is a market with little churn.
segments.tr: The result is a market with little churn.

segments.src: ### A "low-hire, low-fire" market
segments.tr: ### A "low-hire, low-fire" market

segments.src: Economists often describe this pattern as a low-hire, low-fire labor market.
segments.tr: Economists often describe this pattern as a low-hire, low-fire labor market.

segments.src: Workers who have jobs tend to feel relatively secure.
segments.tr: Workers who have jobs tend to feel relatively secure.

segments.src: Workers who are looking for jobs, or who want to switch, find fewer chances.
segments.tr: Workers who are looking for jobs, or who want to switch, find fewer chances.

segments.src: Because people change jobs less often, fewer openings are created by turnover, which makes the search feel harder even when layoffs are rare.
segments.tr: Because people change jobs less often, fewer openings are created by turnover, which makes the search feel harder even when layoffs are rare.

segments.src: ### The experience is uneven
segments.tr: ### The experience is uneven

segments.tr: National averages can hide big differences.

segments.src: Some industries and regions hire steadily while others are cutting back.
segments.tr: Some industries and regions hire steadily while others are cutting back.

segments.src: ## Indicators that give a fuller picture

segments.src: These are commonly used alongside jobless claims:
segments.tr: These are commonly used alongside jobless claims:

segments.src: 1. **Continuing claims.** This measures people who are still receiving benefits after an initial claim. When continuing claims rise while initial claims stay low, it can mean laid-off workers are taking longer to find new jobs.
segments.tr: 1. **Continuing claims.** This measures people who are still receiving benefits after an initial claim. When continuing claims rise while initial claims stay low, it can mean laid-off workers are taking longer to find new jobs.

segments.src: 2. **Job openings and labor turnover (JOLTS).** The Bureau of Labor Statistics survey reports openings, hires, quits, and layoffs. The *hires rate* and the *quits rate* are especially useful for judging how dynamic the market is.
segments.tr: 2. **Job openings and labor turnover (JOLTS).** The Bureau of Labor Statistics survey reports openings, hires, quits, and layoffs. The *hires rate* and the *quits rate* are especially useful for judging how dynamic the market is.

segments.src: 3. **Monthly payroll employment.** The jobs report shows net job growth. Pay attention to revisions, since early estimates are often adjusted later.
segments.tr: 3. **Monthly payroll employment.** The jobs report shows net job growth. Pay attention to revisions, since early estimates are often adjusted later.

segments.src: 4. **The unemployment rate and its duration breakdown.** A rising share of long-term unemployed workers suggests that finding work is getting harder, even if the overall rate looks stable.
segments.tr: 4. **The unemployment rate and its duration breakdown.** A rising share of long-term unemployed workers suggests that finding work is getting harder, even if the overall rate looks stable.

segments.src: 5. **Labor force participation and the employment-population ratio.** These show whether people are working or looking, or have stepped away from the market.
segments.tr: 5. **Labor force participation and the employment-population ratio.** These show whether people are working or looking, or have stepped away from the market.

segments.src: 6. **Wage growth.** Measures such as the Employment Cost Index and average hourly earnings indicate whether employers are competing for workers.
segments.tr: 6. **Wage growth.** Measures such as the Employment Cost Index and average hourly earnings indicate whether employers are competing for workers.

segments.src: 7. **Surveys of workers and employers.** Consumer confidence surveys often ask whether jobs are "plentiful" or "hard to get," and business surveys ask about hiring plans. These capture sentiment that hard counts miss.
segments.tr: 7. **Surveys of workers and employers.** Consumer confidence surveys often ask whether jobs are "plentiful" or "hard to get," and business surveys ask about hiring plans. These capture sentiment that hard counts miss.

segments.src: ## How to read the numbers without overreacting
segments.tr: ## How to read the numbers without overreacting

segments.src: - **Look at trends, not single weeks.** Weekly claims are noisy. Holidays, seasonal patterns, and local events such as weather or a plant closure can shift a single reading. A four-week average smooths some of this out.
segments.tr: - **Look at trends, not single weeks.** Weekly claims are noisy. Holidays, seasonal patterns, and local events such as weather or a plant closure can shift a single reading. A four-week average smooths some of this out.

segments.src: - **Compare across indicators.** If claims are low but hires and quits are also low, the market is probably stable but stagnant, not strong.
segments.tr: - **Compare across indicators.** If claims are low but hires and quits are also low, the market is probably stable but stagnant, not strong.

segments.src: - **Remember that "low" is relative.** The labor force is much larger than in past decades, so a low count of claims should be viewed alongside the size of the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Remember that "low" is relative.** The labor force is much larger than in past decades, so a low count of claims should be viewed alongside the size of the workforce.

segments.src: - **Expect revisions.** Many labor statistics are revised after first publication, and the story can change.
segments.tr: - **Expect revisions.** Many labor statistics are revised after first publication, and the story can change.

segments.src: ## What this means for job seekers and workers
segments.tr: ## What this means for job seekers and workers

segments.src: Low layoffs are good news for people who are currently employed, but they do not guarantee that the search for a new role will be quick.
segments.tr: Low layoffs are good news for people who are currently employed, but they do not guarantee that the search for a new role will be quick.

segments.src: If you are looking for work, some practical steps may help:
segments.tr: If you are looking for work, some practical steps may help:

segments.src: - Focus on sectors and regions where hiring data shows real activity.
segments.tr: - Focus on sectors and regions where hiring data shows real activity.

segments.src: - Expect longer timelines and plan your finances accordingly.
segments.tr: - Expect longer timelines and plan your finances accordingly.

segments.src: - Keep skills and professional networks current, since many openings are filled through referrals.
segments.tr: - Keep skills and professional networks current, since many openings are filled through referrals.

segments.src: - Consider the full compensation picture, not just the headline salary, when weighing offers.
segments.tr: - Consider the full compensation picture, not just the headline salary, when weighing offers.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## The bottom line

segments.src: Jobless claims are a useful early warning for layoffs, and a very low reading signals that employers are not shedding workers in large numbers.
segments.tr: Jobless claims are a useful early warning for layoffs, and a very low reading signals that employers are not shedding workers in large numbers.

segments.src: But a healthy-looking claims figure and a sluggish hiring environment are not contradictory.
segments.tr: But a healthy-looking claims figure and a sluggish hiring environment are not contradictory.

segments.src: To judge how the job market is really doing, look at claims together with hires, quits, openings, duration of unemployment, and wage trends.
segments.tr: To judge how the job market is really doing, look at claims together with hires, quits, openings, duration of unemployment, and wage trends.
